title: Hamilton Water Reclamation Facility
warnings: THE PERMIT'S OWN PAGE COUNT DOES NOT MATCH THE PDF. Sheet 1 prints "Total Pages: 48", but the committed PDF has 47 pages and the last page's own printed header reads "Page 47" — there is no page 48 anywhere in the file, numbered or not. Either the printed total is simply wrong by one, or a 48th page exists in the original instrument and was not captured into this PDF. This corpus cannot distinguish those two possibilities; it is recorded here as a finding, not resolved.

THIS PERMIT HAS ONLY ONE OUTFALL, 1PE00002001, and it carries BOTH the technology-based limits (TSS, CBOD, oil & grease) AND the water-quality-based limits (ammonia, phosphorus monitoring, E. coli, chlorine, B2EHP, whole effluent toxicity monitoring, pH) at the same point. There is no second "001/002" split of technology- vs water-quality-based limits the way some sister facilities in this corpus are built. Anyone expecting a 002 table in this permit will not find one.

THE ONLY SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE BETWEEN THE INITIAL AND FINAL TABLES IS BIS(2-ETHYLHEXYL) PHTHALATE (B2EHP). This was confirmed programmatically (a parameter-by-parameter diff of the two tables' extracted text, after stripping page headers/footers) as well as by reading both tables end to end: every other parameter — TSS, CBOD, oil & grease, ammonia (both seasons), TKN, nitrite+nitrate, phosphorus, orthophosphate, the metals suite, E. coli, chlorine, mercury, free cyanide, both toxicity species, pH, total filterable residue, flow rate — is byte-identical in both tables. B2EHP goes from MONITOR ONLY (all dashes, Initial table) to a numeric limit (maximum 2100 ug/l, monthly average 7.7 ug/l, load 255 kg/day daily / 0.933 kg/day monthly, Final table).

THE B2EHP COMPLIANCE DEADLINE AND THE NEW LIMIT'S ENFORCEABILITY DATE APPEAR TO LAND ON THE SAME DAY, WITH NO MARGIN. Part I.C.B.3 requires compliance with the final B2EHP limits "no later than 36 months after the effective date of this permit" — a plain duration, which from 2021-11-01 computes to 2024-11-01. Part I.A.2 separately says the Final table (carrying that same B2EHP limit) applies "beginning on the 37th month after effective date" — an ordinal-month phrase that, read the same way the "36th month"/"37th month" language resolves elsewhere in this corpus (month 1 = the effective date's own calendar month), also lands on 2024-11-01. Both resolutions are [inference]: the permit prints neither date, only the duration/ordinal language. If the reading is right, the permittee's deadline to already BE compliant is the identical calendar date the limit first becomes legally enforceable — effectively zero buffer, unlike a schedule that gives a facility a running-start margin before its own new limit bites.

EVERY SCHEDULE-OF-COMPLIANCE DEADLINE IN THIS PERMIT HAS ALREADY PASSED, AND SO HAS THE PERMIT'S OWN RENEWAL-APPLICATION DEADLINE. As of 2026-08-26: the pretreatment local-limits justification (6 months, ~2022-05-01), the Phosphorus Optimization plan and the first B2EHP report (12 months, ~2022-11-01), the second B2EHP progress report (24 months, ~2023-11-01), B2EHP compliance itself (36 months, ~2024-11-01), and the Storm Water "No Exposure Certification" re-affirmation (an explicit calendar date printed on the permit: 2024-03-15) are all in the past. More urgently: the permit's own 180-day renewal-application deadline ahead of its 2026-10-31 expiration — on or about 2026-05-04 — has ALSO passed, and the permit itself expires in roughly two months from today. Nothing in this corpus establishes whether any of these were filed — no submittal, no acknowledgment, no renewal application, no ECHO/ICIS extract for this facility is committed. "Past due" here means only that the date has passed, NOT that the City of Hamilton missed it or that the permit is lapsing without a pending renewal.

THE TABLE CAPTIONS IN THE TEXT LAYER READ AS DUPLICATED: "Table - Final Outfall - 001 - Initial - 001 - Initial" for the Initial table and "Table - Final Outfall - 001 - Final - 001 - Final" for the Final table. This may be the permit's own printed caption or an artifact of how pypdf linearizes a merged/multi-row table header cell; it does not affect any transcribed limit value, and it was not checked against a render (see method above). Transcribed here verbatim rather than silently cleaned up.

THIS PERMIT NAMES NO COMBINED SEWER OVERFLOW PARTS. The authorization sentence on sheet 1 limits itself to "Parts I, II, and III of this permit" — there is no Part IV/V/VI here, and Part II Item D's SSO definition explicitly carves out "wet weather discharges from combined sewer overflows specifically listed in Part II of this NPDES permit (if any)" — the "(if any)" is boilerplate; no CSO station or CSO limits appear anywhere in this document.

THE BYPASS STATION CARRIES NO NUMERIC LIMITS AND NO FLOW-BASED TRIGGER. Station 1PE00002603 (Part I.B.6) is monitor-only on every parameter — TSS, ammonia and CBOD carry no limit, only "When Disch. Grab All." Discharge through it is simply "prohibited," full stop, with enforcement waived only under the general three-part defense at 40 CFR 122.41(m) / Part III Item 11.C.1. There is no permit-specific numeric precondition (e.g. a sustained-flow threshold) governing when the bypass may be used.

THE SSO NOTE'S OWN PREMISE CONTRADICTS ITS OWN TABLE, AT BOTH SSO STATIONS. Note a for both 1PE00002027 (sheet 10) and 1PE00002037 (sheet 11) opens: "Although the above table indicates that the Measuring Frequency for Overflow Occurrence is 1/Month..." But the table it refers to prints "When Disch. Total" in the Measuring Frequency cell for Overflow Occurrence (code 74062) at both stations — not "1/Month" (see monitoring_stations.sso_027.parameters.overflow_occurrence.monitoring above, transcribed verbatim from the table; "No./Month" there is only the reporting UNIT, not a measuring frequency). The note's stated premise does not match the table it is describing. Both halves are already transcribed elsewhere in this file; recorded here as an unresolved internal disagreement rather than silently favoring either reading.

THE SAME ASTM STANDARD IS PRINTED TWO WAYS IN THIS PERMIT. Part I.C, Item A.4.b (sheet 23, Sampling Methods) lists "ASTM D7237" among the approved free-cyanide domestic-background methods, with no revision suffix. Part II, Item T (sheet 29) lists the same method as "ASTM D7237-10." Both are printed exactly as quoted here on their own sheet; this corpus does not resolve whether the permit means the same edition of the standard in both places or whether the omission on sheet 23 is simply informal.

THREE PRINTED TYPOS, TRANSCRIBED VERBATIM RATHER THAN SILENTLY CORRECTED. (1) Sheet 19's upstream monitoring table (station 1PE00002801) prints parameter 61435 as "96-Hr. Acute Toxicity Pimephales promela" — missing the terminal "s" (the correct species name, Pimephales promelas, is printed correctly elsewhere in this same permit, e.g. parameter 61428). (2) Sheet 11, SSO note c for station 1PE00002037, prints "All sanitary sewer overflowsare prohibited" — "overflows" and "are" are run together with no space; sheet 10's note c for station 1PE00002027 prints the same sentence correctly spaced. (3) Sheet 30, Item Y.2 (Acute Bioassays) prints "annual acute toxicity tests using Ceriodaphnia dubia semi-annual acute toxicity tests using fathead minnows" — dropping the conjunction between the two clauses (almost certainly "and," between "dubia" and "semi-annual," was intended). None of the three affects a numeric limit or a monitoring requirement; recorded here per the corpus's transcribe-as-printed convention.

title: City of Middletown Wastewater Treatment Works
warnings: THE OUTFALL NUMBER IS BLANK IN THE PART I.A.2 AUTHORIZATION SENTENCE ON ITS FACE, and this was checked against a 300 DPI render of sheet 5 (see header note) rather than assumed from the text layer. The sentence reads "...the permittee is authorized to discharge in accordance with the following limitations and monitoring requirements from the following outfall: 1PE00003 . See Part II, OTHER REQUIREMENTS, for locations of effluent sampling." — the expected "001" suffix simply is not printed between "1PE00003" and the period. The parallel sentence introducing the Initial-period table (sheet 2) prints the full "1PE00003001" without defect. Every other reference to the outfall in this permit (the table captions, Item C, Item D, the compliance schedule) prints the full eight-digit number; only this one sentence is short.

THE PRINTED PAGE NUMBERING SKIPS "PAGE 20", AND THE STATION THAT WOULD LOGICALLY SIT THERE IS MISSING FROM THE PERMIT. PDF page index 18 is printed "Page 19" (the Part I.B.9 Downstream-Farfield table, station 901); PDF page index 19 — the very next physical page — is printed "Page 21" and is BYTE-IDENTICAL in body text to "Page 19" (confirmed by direct text comparison, not by page-number reading alone). No physical page anywhere in this PDF is printed "Page 20"; the sequence goes 1-19, 21-81, which is 80 distinct printed numbers matching the PDF's actual 80 pages — see pdf_vs_printed_pages below. nine_minimum_controls.preamble: "The entire wastewater treatment system shall be operated and maintained so that the total loading of pollutants discharged during wet weather is minimized."
nine_minimum_controls.controls: 1. Proper O&M of the collection system and CSO points. 2. Maximize collection-system storage of wet-weather flow before overflow. 3. Review/modify the pretreatment program to minimize nondomestic-discharge impact from CSOs. 4. Maximize the POTW's wet-weather treatment capability within its limits. 5. Prohibit dry-weather overflows. 6. Control solid/floatable materials in CSO discharge. 7. Required CSO inspection, monitoring and reporting. 8. Pollution-prevention programs targeting CSO contaminant levels. 9. Public notification program for CSO-affected areas, especially beaches/recreation areas.

quantification_levels.compliance_rule: Maximum limits: any value reported below the OEPA QL is in compliance. Average limits: compliance is the arithmetic mean using zero for values below the QL, compared to the average limit. Signature/Plan Review (30-day correction window on Director notice of deficiency). I. Keeping SWPPP Current. J. Contents of SWPPP (pollution prevention team, potential-pollutant-source description, site map requirements, control-measure description, schedules, monitoring/inspection documentation, substantially-identical-outfall documentation, recordkeeping — public availability subject to CBI withholding). K. Sector-Specific Requirements — Sector T (Treatment Works): non-storm-water discharge prohibition (sanitary/industrial wastewater, equipment/vehicle washwater); additional BMPs for grit/screenings/solids handling, sludge drying beds/piles, compost piles, septage/hauled-waste receiving; additional employee-training topics; additional SWPPP site-map and pollutant-source documentation for those same areas plus access roads/rail lines; additional inspection scope for the same areas; and a requirement to keep current NPDES washwater permits (or pending applications) with the SWPPP.
